delthuntle: Delthuntle was a commercial center and port in Aglarond. The city suffered from some difficulty with pirates that patrol the coastline. * Morada Topolino, mansion belonging to Pericolo Topolino.
furthinghome: Furthinghome was a trading port city in Aglarond and one of the oldest cities in the nation. Around 1368 DR, it was made up of some buildings in the traditional Aglarondan weathered wood style and others made from stone.
athkatla: {{Location The streets of Athkatla were well lit in the evenings, thanks to the massive, halfling-sized street oil lamps known as "storm-lanterns".
crimmor: {{Location Built on the southern shore of the Alandor River, Crimmor was a city constantly bustling with life. Traveling towards the north was difficult, as the soft river bottom made it hard to build bridges.
eshpurta: Eshpurta, the "Shield City" of Amn, was a bustling military trade town in eastern Amn. which downgraded the once-thriving metropolis to a large city.
esmeltaran: Esmeltaran was a large city in central Amn that served as its capital for much of its history. It was famed for its beautiful architecture, opulent resorts, and warm, pleasant weather.
imnescar: {{Location Imnescar was considered an agricultural center for the nation's south and was famous for its fruits. These included oranges, tangerines, grapes, dates, lemons, limes, avocados, and artichokes.
keczulla: The city of Keczulla was a prosperous city that was the home of diverse and rich mining industry. The town stood on the the Eshpurta Road, to the east from Amnwater and west of Eshpurta.
murann: Murann, known as the Sailors' City, was a port city and the second-largest city of Amn and became the capital of the newly established kingdom of Muranndin.
nashkel: {{Location Circa 1357 DR and through 1370 DR, Nashkel had a population of around 4,500 people, with 3,000 based in the town itself and 1,500 in the outer farms and villages.
purskul: {{Location Circa 1370 DR, Purskul was recorded as having a population of around 12,000 people, comprising 40% humans, 30% halflings, 29% half-orcs, and 1% full-blooded orcs.
riatavin: {{Location A group of merchants known as the Chosen Council governed the city in the 15th century DR. The city was primarily defended by the Ring Knights of Riatavin, a force of mounted troops armed with longswords, shields, and rods, adorned in chainmail armor.
ascore: {{Location In its heyday, Ascore was a wealthy and bustling port on the Narrow Sea, standing as the gateway to Delzoun. Here dwarves traded with elves of Eaerlann and Myth Drannor and humans of Netheril and Nimbral.
yallasch: {{Location Yallasch imported wares and crops from neighboring Adaerglast. The sinister wizards Iraun and Srivven installed themselves as absolute rulers in the nearby realm of Adaerglast, and before long they also set their sights on Yallasch.
almraiven: Almraiven was one of the great cities of the nation of Calimshan. It was most notable for being the nation's first and premier center for magical studies, until the late 15 century DR, when the region's enslaved populace rose up and overthrew their tyrannical genie-kin rulers.
calimport: {{Location {{quote|…I care about Calimport as much as I care not to step on a viper.
memnon: Memnon was a key port of trade and garrison city for the kingdom of Calimshan. capital of the efreet kingdom of Memnonnar. it became the capital of a reborn Memnonnar, ruled by genies and genasi.
schamedar: {{Location The city contained only four sabbans. The northern-most sabban was Bakkal's Sabban, where the upper classes lived. This was also where the most ornate temples were located.
suldolphor: Suldolphor, which was also called Suldolphor the Golden or simply the Golden City, was a metropolis found in far eastern Calimshan. Suldolphor lay along the western banks of the strait called Talagath's Gauntlet, in between the Lake of Steam and the Shining Sea, making it the easternmost city in Calimshan.
akanax: Akanax was a harsh, warlike city in the Akanal region of Chessenta known for its talented smiths, its rigid military structure, and its intolerance of outsiders.
cimbar: Cimbar was a city-state in the Old Empires and a sometimes-capital of the empire of Chessenta. Cimbar was ruled by a leader called a Sceptanar, In 1154 DR, Cimbar was put under siege by the city-states of Akanax and Soorenar.
luthcheq: Luthcheq was the capital city of Chessenta. Formerly a port city located on the Bay of Chessenta, as of 1479 DR the city was miles from what remained of the bay.
mordulkin: Mordulkin was the center of worship in Chessenta of the Mulhorandi god Anhur, the God of Might and Warrior of the South. His worship had been brought back and spread by Chessentan mercenaries, and he was seen as more of a southern god than a specifically Mulhorandi one.
arrabar: {{Location The sleepy city was an ancient and sprawling megapolis, though the people kept it tidy, clean, and maintained. One of the most distinctive features of Arrabar was greenery.
hlath: {{Location Hlath was an old walled city with streets of cobblestone that veered between mostly four and five-story buildings. The city walls rose up.
iljak: {{Location Iljak was ruled by the governor, who, in turn, was controlled by Chondath. In the late-14 century DR, Iljak was ruled by Governor Anton Yinoran.
mussum: Mussum was an abandoned city in Chondath, lying on the southeast shore of the Vilhon Reach. It was a plague-ridden ruin, but also home to the House of Holy Suffering, a major temple to Ilmater.
shamph: Shamph, also known as the Crossroads City, was a city in the nation of Chondath in the Vilhon Reach. Merchants from the south stopped at Shamph to sell their goods to avoid the war zone between the cities of Iljak and Hlath.
fort beluarian: {{Location As of the late 15 century DR, Beluarian Flaming Fist members offered hired adventurers to perform certain tasks to aid their efforts. These included expeditions to hunt the undead in the heart of the jungle and reconnaissance missions to explore remote locations or mysterious happenings.
mezro: {{Location This quarter was located in the southwest. It was a literal maze of simple, one-story, adobe-style houses. Most Mezroans lived here.
arabel: {{Location Arabel was at the junction of the High Road, Calantar's Way, the East Way, and the Moonsea Ride. The farming town of Clarkswell was located fifty miles north of Arabel, in the foothills of the Storm Horn Mountains.
daerlun: Daerlun was a large city in Sembia. The city declared itself a neutral independent city-state in the , rather than be absorbed by Cormyr or stay under the direct influence of Sembia.
elversult: ) was a rich community found in the Dragon Coast region of Faerûn. It was an important trading and mercantile center that facilitated both honest and illegitimate trade across the Eastern Heartlands and beyond.
marsember: Marsember ( ), also known as the City of Spices }} The city lay on sandy islands in the swampy west bank of the mouth of the Starwater River. As it was a city of trade, its design made use of canals that doubled as open sewers.
pros: {{Location WestDragonCoast.png|1479 DR Elversult.JPG|1372 DR Even before it fell into ruin, Pros was not the most beauteous locale. Its buildings were in great disrepair, and its "port" had only a few rickety docks that could not support larger vessels.
proskur: ) was a trading city in Cormyr, that was located south of the kingdom's traditional borders, in the Dragon Coast region of the Eastern Heartlands. While it had become a place known for honest and fair trade, To the northwest of Proskur was located the fortification of Stormhawk Keep.
suzail: Suzail ( ) was the capital of Cormyr and the seat of power. It was named after Suzara Obarskyr, the mother of the first king. It was originally the farm of Ondeth Obarskyr, the father of the first king.
teziir: ) was a protectorate of Cormyr, The city was still considered a frontier town by most people. Its growth had been haphazard. They had a poor reputation as an exceptionally indolent and inept fighting force.
tilverton: {{Location Tilverton was traditionally governed by a council of elected citizens, which for a time was effectively led by a charismatic and popular priest of Gond named Gharri.
urmlaspyr: Urmlaspyr ( ) was a city in southern Sembia that was notable mostly for its poor treatment at the hands of the shadovar. The city was supported by Cormyr and a significant amount of trade from that country flowed through its port.
ashabenford: {{Location Composed of rustic homes and collections of cottages, Ashabenford sat on the eastern side of the River Ashaba, though some of its notable buildings were found also on the west bank.
essembra: ) was the largest town and center of trade in Battledale, The town itself was deep in the forest of Cormanthyr: the trees of the Elven Court woods hemmed Essembra on all sides.
cathyr: Cathyr (also seen as Cathtyr) was a metropolis and the capital city of Dambrath. It was formerly known as Shantil. Cathyr sat in a small bay on the far eastern end of Dambrath.
delzimmer: Delzimmer was a city in southeast Faerûn that began as a landlocked trading center, but became a port for shipping after the Spellplague caused the Gulf of Luiren to form as the Great Sea filled in the lowlands practically to its doorstep.
maarlith: {{Location Maarlith was located in central Dambrath in the southern reaches of the Rialuil Plain on the northern coast of the Bay of Dancing Dolphins.
halagard: Halagard was a city located in central Halruaa. At 7,500 inhabitants, Halagard sported a large population when compared to other Halruaan cities.
halarahh: {{Location The city was made of pink coral houses; towers of white, blue, or green marble, crystal, and stone; streets cobbled in semiprecious stone, and fanciful fountains filled the air with fresh splashes and bubbles.
ormpur: {{Location thumb|left|A map of Lapaliiya, showing Ormpur at the northern edge. The city stood at the eastern tip of the Shining Sea, at the head of Ormpur Bay It lay at the northwestern end of the range called the Wormbones and the edge of the Shaar Ormpur was named the City of Saffron
loudwater: {{Location It was also once home to a community of elves, part of the nation of Eaerlann As recorded in their own histories, two elven houses established themselves here as they built a school of philosophy, which they named the Velti'Enorethal.
mithral hall: King Obould Many-arrows launched an attack on Mithral Hall in 1370 DR with a huge army of orcs. The staggering army came from the Spine of the World.
dilpur: {{Location Dilpur was a rather insignificant location until its population swelled with refugees. After the influx of citizens, plans were quickly made to construct new city walls and expand the docks.
hlammach: {{Location Like many of Impiltur's grand cities, Hlammach was free from slums and poverty for a great many years, Hlammach was a compact, walled-city that had a grand port that was nearly always full of ships.
ilmwatch: {{Location Despite its strategic location between Impiltur and Damara, Ilmwatch was not a particularly busy port city. Ilmwatch was founded by Ilmara, sister of Imbrar I, during his brief rule.
lyrabar: {{Location The city was long and narrow, stretching over a mile along the northern coast of the Sea of Fallen Stars. In the Year of the Ormserpent, 1295 DR, the capital city of Dilpur was sacked during the Prince's Revolt.
sarshel: {{Location * Marhymbel House Shipways, one of the fastest ship-builders in the Sea of Fallen Stars, led by brothers Ilund and Vromur Marhymbel in the 1490s DR.
telflamm: {{Location Shemszarr Square was at the center of the city's commerce. Many of its merchants and trading company headquarters were located around the square, including the Thayan Enclave.
derlusk: Derlusk was a city of music that grew up around one of the busiest harbors in the Border Kingdoms southeast of the Dragonsmoke Ridge. Evidence of Wealth was everywhere in the city, with many of the stout stone buildings appearing as a beautiful vista of slate roofs and shimmering lanterns at night.
innarlith: Innarlith was a city-state located on the eastern tip of the Lake of Steam in south Faerûn. thumb|The location of Innarlith on the Lake of Steam.
anchoril: Anchoril was a town on the island of Suj, located on its eastern shores, washed with the waters of the Trackless Sea. The closest major settlement to Anchoril was Sujjar, west of Anchoril, built on the Suj-lan bay.

beluir: {{Location Beluir was established by Halflings in 14 DR. In 1105 DR, a powerful storm from the Great Sea destroyed most of the city, but it was rebuilt.
chethel: Chethel was a coastal city in the halfling realm of Luiren. The city was founded in 47 DR. In 1105 DR, the city received widespread damage from a storm over the Great Sea.
shoun: {{Location Melino Richtoes was the mayor of Shoun in 1367 DR. Shoun was founded by halflings in 116 DR. The settlement sported a host of bakeries, eventually giving rise to the phrase "fat as a Shounite" throughout Luiren.
thruldar: Thruldar, the most westerly outpost of Estagund, was found on the border of Luiren, on the edge of the Lluirwood. It was located along the trade route which ran from Estagund and Durpar west to Delzimmer in northern Luiren in the lands between the Lluirwood and the Toadsquat Mountains .
citadel of the raven: The Citadel of the Raven was a fortress of the Zhentarim that was situated within the Dragonspine Mountains in the western portion of the Moonsea region. The Citadel itself was the main feature of the stronghold, which rested in the center of 10 miles (16 km) of interconnected fortresses on the western end of the Drago
elmwood: {{Location Elmwood's merchant area was located in the center of the village. ;Docks: Busiest part of the village located on the northern part of Elmwood; it was made by a series of wooden docks and piers where both village boats and passing merchant vessels moored.
elventree: {{Location Elventree had been built up with wood on ruins of stone buildings. There was an elegant but natural-looking palace. There were also a number of structures in the branches of trees, which were linked by rope ladders, walkways, and bridges of silver rope and white planks.
hillsfar: Hillsfar was a powerful city-state located on the southern coast of the Moonsea. The city was heavily involved in trade in the region, acting as a hub for cities and settlements in the surrounding area.
hulburg: {{Location In the mid-to-late 14 century DR, the city lay in ruins with few other than the Hulmaster family residing within the derelict city itself.
melvaunt: ), also known as the City of Swords, was a frontier city that sat on the northern coast of the Moonsea, in the Moonsea North region of north Faerûn. It was a city of smithing and mercantile services, as well as factories serving as the port of entry to many travelers coming to the region.
mulmaster: Mulmaster ( ), also known as the City of Danger, was an independent city-state in the harsh Moonsea region of northern Faerûn.
phlan: Phlan, also known as the Jewel of the Moonsea, was a large frontier town on the Moonsea region of north Faerûn with a long and storied history.
teshwave: {{Location {{quote|Teshwave has approximately fifty native citizens left, and they are unable to leave because they have nowhere else to go. The fight has gone out of the people; they accept their lot like dumb sheep.
thentia: {{Location Thentia.png|1480 DR Melvaunt.JPG|1372 DR Thentia was considered to have an unrestrained albeit disorderly spirit, without the ever-present malice harbored by some cities of the Moonsea.
zhentil keep: Zhentil Keep ( ), also called Thargate Keep, Along with the Citadel of the Raven, Zhentil Keep was destroyed by the Shadovar in 1383 DR during the Shadowbane War.
gheldaneth: Gheldaneth was the second largest city in the nation of Mulhorand, as well as one of its sixteen preceptual governments. It would later come to be the only city in Mulhorand to survive the Spellplague after 1385 DR.
skuld: Skuld was located on the coast of the Alamber Sea. Prior to the Spellplague, Skuld was the capital city of the nation of Mulhorand. The City of Eternity, as it was also known, was claimed to be the oldest inhabited settlement in Faerûn, and, before its destruction, was certainly the largest.
sultim: {{Location Sultim was located in northern Mulhorand within a region of high plains called the Taranoth. It sat along the coast of the Alamber Sea due west from the Ganathwood.
bildoobaris: {{Location Though certainly not a permanent location, the Trade Fair was home to upwards of 30,000 Nar every summer as members of the various tribes meet on the vast plains.
jiyyd: {{Location Jiyyd's position as a crossroads between the Long Road and Peltarch made it a major site of trade and barter between the Nars and foreigners.
n'jast: {{Location The village was predominantly a trade outpost. Merchants on the Long Road came from Damara in the west and Rashemen in the east, while merchants on the Cold Road came from the settlements and dwarfholds of the Icerim Mountains to the north and Thesk to the south.
peltarch: Peltarch was the only permanent town of any size in Narfell as of 1479 DR, with most of the inhabitants being Nars of the Ulyoon tribe. The town was located on the southern shore of Icelace Lake and was constructed from the masonry of Old Peltarch to the north of the current settlement.
immilmar: Immilmar was the capital city of Rashemen and seat of power for the nation's Iron Lord. Beyond its political importance as the heart of Rashemen, it was perhaps most famous for its great crafters, whose goods were renowned across the Unapproachable East and the Cold Lands.
mulptan: {{Location The vast, wind-battered city was encircled by a great stone wall, outside of which was its great trading field. The tents and and stalls found in mercantile marketplace were crowded with people of many different ethnicities and foreign nations.
mulsantir: {{Location {{quote|It is said that Mulsantir has thin boundaries between the Prime and the Plane of Shadow, especially at night or in dark places.
ordulin: ) was the capital of Sembia, until it was destroyed in a planar rift summoned by Elyril Hraven, one of Shar's followers, in 1374 DR. There was a constant ominous cloud above the city, along with a lone earthmote with a Shadovar citadel resting atop it.
saerloon: ), which was once called Chondathan Saerloon has a busy port on the aptly named Saerloon Bay, that bustled with activity late into the night. The city was built on every piece of land that touched the water, hungrily claiming it as too precious to be wasted.
selgaunt: ), formerly known as Chancelgaunt, was a large merchant port on the Sea of Fallen Stars, and for a period following the destruction of Ordulin in the late 14 century DR up until 1499 DR, the interim capital of the nation of Sembia.
elbulder: {{Location Elbulder was the southernmost settlement among the three cities of the Kingdom of Sespech. The city was nestled between two tributaries of the River Arran along the Old Road with a bridge across each.
fort arran: {{Location {{quote|This fort is the Barons first line of defense against an attack launched from Arrabar.
lheshayl: {{Location A long line of chiefs ruled Lheshayl, and in 1372 DR, the city was led by Chief Entawanata. Assam was governed by a ruling council that consisted of representatives from Lheshayl and Ormath.
mimph: {{Location {{quote|I see the scales, jaws, and claws that shout "monster" to most, aye, but I see more than that.
nimpeth: {{Location Most of Nimpeth's city walls and buildings were constructed by slave labor, including the city's seat of power – the Citadel of Carifar.
ormpetarr: {{Location In the 14 century DR, Ormpetarr was ruled by Baron Thuragar Foesmasher, supported by the city's merchants, who stood in dire opposition to the nation of Chondath.
surkh: {{Location Surkh's lizardmen population was considered to be the most advanced and civilized among other lizardfolk settlements of Faerûn. The city was inhabited mainly by lizardfolk and a small number of lizard kings, who kept to themselves.
eartheart: Eartheart was the primary settlement of the gold dwarves in East Rift in the late 15 century DR and their cultural and spiritual heart. It used to house great temples and shrines to all the dwarven pantheon and dwarf heroes but after the great collapse much was lost.
shaarmid: {{Location Shaarmid sat near the center of the vast Shaar. It lay north of Lake Lhespen and south of the Firesteap Mountains. Every four years, in the month of Eleasis, attendees of the Dance of the Shimmering Blades passed through Shaarmid on their way to the festival site.
red larch: The town of Red Larch was a waystop on the Long Road seven days north of Waterdeep, The town was named after a small forest stand of red larches that extended along the ridge.
triboar: {{Location Triboar was nestled in the Dessarin Valley, strategically placed where the Evermoor Way intersected with the Long Road. and 200 miles (321.9 kilometers) north of Red Larch, by way of the Long Road.
waterdeep: Waterdeep, also known as the City of Splendors or the Crown of the North, was the most important and influential city in the North and perhaps in all Faerûn.
darromar: {{Location Darromar, formerly known as Ithmong, was a metropolis and the capital of Tethyr. It lay on the River Ith. Its central location ensured that the queen's armies in 1479 DR were never more than five days' hard ride from any trouble in her domain.
mosstone: Mosstone was a walled caravan-stop town in Tethyr on the Trade Way near the Wealdath forest. The residents referred to themselves as Mosstonians.
myratma: Myratma was one of the most important cities in Tethyr, known around Faerûn for the quality of its textiles, owing to the output from the Tethyr Mills outside its walls.
saradush: {{Location In 1368 DR the fire giant Bhaalspawn Yaga Shura, leading his mercenary army, besieged the city of Saradush, briefly occupied by his weaker siblings and Calishite forces under command of the half-orc Bhaalspawn Gromnir Il-Khan.
velen: Velen was a port city on the Tethyrian peninsula overlooking the Sea of Swords. The coastal city served as the capital of duchy of Cape Velen, within the Kingdom of Tethyr in the 14 century DR and onward into the 15 century after the realm's independence was declared.
zazesspur: {{Location Architecturally and culturally, Zazesspur was an odd mixture of Tethyrian and Calishite influences, with others blended in. Most buildings were several stories tall and constructed of tight-fitting stone.
bezantur:
{{Location thumb|The location of Bezantur in Thay.|400x400px
Bezantur was enclosed within massive, black walls that loomed over its outer streets.
delhumide: Delhumide was a city in the tharch of the same name, located in northeastern Thay. When Thay had been a Mulhorandi colony, around 1000 years before Dale Reckoning, Delhumide was one of its greatest cities and bastions of power.
eltabbar: {{Location The city was the nexus of Thayan slave trade up until the late 14 century DR. Thousands of slaves were shipped into the city before being auctioned off to live out the rest of their short, unfortunate lives.
escalant: Escalant was a coastal city situated on the mouth of the River Lapendrar located within the tharch of same name in the eastern nation of Thay. While it was previously independent and allied with other port city-states in the region, Escalant was intermittently under Thayan control during the 350 years leading up to the
nethentir: {{Location Nethentir was the sister-town of Nethjet, though it never attained the same level of prosperity. Together they served as the starting point for a number of Thayan invasions into the lands of Thesk and Aglarond.
pyarados: Pyarados was a lawless city located in the eastern frontier of Thay. It was a wild city of adventurers that served as a base of operations for those who sought to explore the rugged Sunrise Mountains and lands further east.
surthay: {{Location Most of Surthay reeked of the fetid smell of pestilence, rotten vegetation and swamp water from the nearby Surmarsh, The capital lay outside of the enchantments of the Thayan Plateau that protected the nation from inclement weather.
tyraturos: {{Location The city in the central region of the tharch of Tyraturos north of Bezantur. Tyraturos was founded during an age of expansion of Mulhorand under the leadership of Anhurtep.
khôltar: Khôltar was a small city on the edge of the Great Rift in south Faerûn. It was known as the Iron City because of its high walls covered in iron. and to Shaarmid on the Golden Road about to the west.
luskan: Luskan, also known as the City of Sails, was a port city at the mouth of the River Mirar on the Sword Coast North. }} As of 1370 DR, the city was split into northern and southern halves by the River Mirar, and these were connected by the bridges Dalath's Span, Harbor Cross, and the Upstream Span.
mirabar: Mirabar ( ) was a mining city of great wealth located on the Sword Coast. As of 1368 DR it was the richest city north of Waterdeep. In 1370 DR, the city was occupied by 1600 shield dwarves who lived underground near to their workshops, which produced metal goods for export in the region and beyond.
neverwinter: Neverwinter, also known as the City of Skilled Hands and the Jewel of the North, was a bustling, cultured, and cosmopolitan city-state in northwest Faerûn. Neverwinter was regarded by Volo as the most cosmopolitan and civilized city in all of Faerûn.
silverymoon: Silverymoon, the Welcoming City, was a powerful metropolis in the North and the thriving pinnacle of human culture, even amidst the wilderness of the Savage Frontier.
procampur: Procampur ( Procampur maintained a strong defense force of army and navy, primarily to protect its valuable gem and metal trade from pirates and rival states.
ravens bluff: {{Location During the late 14 century DR, Ravens Bluff was a rapidly-growing, young city, rife with opportunities for adventure to be found, intrigue to be unraveled and riches to be earned.
tantras: {{Location During the Vast's so-called Time of Glorious Fools (from 649 DR onwards), Tantras was among those harbors that served as landing spots for immigrants and rest stops for pirates.
tsurlagol: {{Location It was a prosperous port city, the last on the Inner Sea before Impiltur. The name "Tsurlagol" was pronounced as Tsss-SIR-lah-gol or TSIR-lah-gol, and its people were called "Tsurlagoli".
westgate: {{Location Westgate was a seedy and squalid metropolis—with a history in piracy, powerful crime syndicates, and nameless vampiric crime-lords. Westgate thrived on black-market trade and corruption, and was perhaps one of the most sordid cities in all of Faerûn.
nethjet: {{Location Marek Rymüt was native to this city and received training in magic to be a Red Wizard at a magic school located there in the early 14 century DR.
nyth: {{Location It was once controlled by the independent city-state of Telflamm, but it was a part of Thesk by 1372 DR. It traded with its fellow cities of Thesk and with Telflamm.
phsant: {{Location Some time in the early 14 century DR, Hargrid Tenslayer killed the child of the hierarch of Phsant and was driven out of the city. In the , the advancing Tuigan Horde laid siege to Phsant and swiftly conquered it on Kythorn 20, and the Tuigan sacked Phsant.
tammar: Tammar was a large town in Thesk. As of 1372 DR, it had a population of 3,594. It was razed by the Tuigan Horde and subsequently besieged by bandits who took heavy tolls from passing caravans.
alaghôn: {{Location The ancient port city channeled nearly all the trade that Turmish had with the rest of Faerûn for centuries, It was the most popular port on the southern fringes of the Inner Sea.
gildenglade: {{Location Gildenglade was built at the base of the Aphrunn Mountains, not far from the Lake of Drifting Stars to the north. The city was connected to Halondar, or the Turmway, by two major roads that ran from Gildenglade north towards the trade route.
hlondeth: {{Location Hlondeth was a well-run, organized, and efficient walled city-state. and natural sources. After dark, the view of the city was reflected off the waters of the Vilhon Reach.
morningstar hollows: Morningstar Hollows once was a small fishing village, abandoned due to the continual flooding of the Alaoreum River. The boggy village bacame home to a tribe of lizardfolk.
nonthal: Nonthal was a city, reputed for being the most peaceful and stable in the nation of Turmish, in the Vilhon Reach. The city had a functioning sewer system, that was fixed, expanded, and improved by Joster Barbellow, of the Barbellow gnome family.
starmantle: Starmantle, referred to as the Ruins of Starmantle during the century that followed the Spellplague, was once a small, coastal city that was located on the Dragon Coast, up until the late 14 century DR, Starmantle had an analogous city in the Shadowfell known as Elgrin Fau.
messemprar: {{Location By 1479 DR, Messemprar's ruins were inhabited by sahuagin.
shussel: Shussel was a small city on the northern shore of the Alamber Sea, in Unther. Shussel served was fishing town, however it used to be a mining outpost at some point of its history.
unthalass: {{Location Unthalass was populated mostly by humans of the Mulan ethnic group, most of them nobles. After the destruction of Unther, the ruins of Unthalass were inhabited by lamias.
bloodstone village: {{Location In 1347 DR, Bloodstone Village was ravaged by the harsh Wolf Winter, during which their crops died and starving dire wolves killed 70 of the village's inhabitants.
darmshall: {{Location Darmshall was surrounded by farmland and ranches, The city sat in the north of the Sunderland, a region of southeastern Vaasa, in the foothills of the Galena Mountains.
ilinvur: {{Location In the mid–14 century DR, Ilinvur comprised about 6000 residents and was governed by a mage installed jointly by Melvaunt and Thentia who was assisted by twenty heavily armed Keepers of the Peace.
nesmé: Nesmé ( ) was a small frontier city located in the Savage Frontier of northwest Faerûn. Nesmé sat beside the River Subrin. The dangerous Lurkwood forest rested in the north.
palischuk: {{Location The city was a fortress town rebuilt in the mid-to-late 14 century DR by half-orcs It was made of up mostly shorter buildings and was well-lit at night by torchlight.
assam: {{Location Assam was a wallless town on the endless wide plains, drowning in circling packs of herd animals and numerous caravans. The city smelled of tanneries and slaughterhouses, appropriately for its main trade.
ormath: {{Location There was a temple to Tempus in the city, which may or may not have any connection with the phrase "Ormath on the warpath", commonly used to describe the city.
reth: {{Location Reth was a high-walled The amphitheater was used as a gladiatorial arena that hosted battles twice per tenday. The Gap of Reth was located behind a sizable gate that protected the city from dangers of the savage inhabitants of the Akanapeaks.
sapra: {{Location The city welcomed those who wanted to flee oppression by wizards. Sapra aided refugees from the lands ruled by spell-casting tyrants, and its inhabitants even included several "retired" Red Wizards who fled Thay.
asbravn: ) was a small town found in the Western Heartlands. Asbravn lay in a shallow valley in between the Dusk Road and the Uldoon Trail.
baldur's gate: Baldur's Gate, called the City of Blood was one of the largest metropolises and city-states on the Sword Coast, within the greater Western Heartlands. It was a crowded city of commerce and opportunity, and one of the most prosperous and influential merchant cities on the western coast of Faerûn.
berdusk: Berdusk was known as the Jewel of the Vale as it sat on both the Uldoon Trail and the River Chionthar in Sunset Vale. Twilight Hall was located here, making the city the base of many operations for Harpers in the west and the north.
beregost: ) was a town on the Coast Way, halfway between Baldur's Gate and Amn. It was a popular stop for many visiting merchant caravans, especially those en route to Waterdeep in the north or to the Sea of Fallen Stars in the east.
candlekeep: Candlekeep was the famous library-fortress that stood proud as a bastion of enlightenment and knowledge on the Sword Coast for many centuries. It housed a magnificent collection of books and scrolls of lore, considered the greatest collection of the writings in all of Faerûn.
corm orp: Corm Orp was a small town in the Western Heartlands on the Dusk Road. In the mid–14 century DR, it was dominated by halflings and led by a human mayor. It was the fastest-growing settlement of halflings north of Luiren.
daggerford: {{Location Surrounding the town wall was a modest moat, with three crossing points at each of the town's three gates — the Farmer's Gate in the north, the Caravan Gate in the west, and the River Gate in the south.
elturel: {{Location In the mid–14 century DR, the people of the region spoke the Thorasta language, which was related to Chondathan. People and things from here were called "Elturian", while "Elturelian" was considered incorrect.
evereska: Evereska ( , Elvish for "fortress home") was a secreted city within a fabled valley in the Western Heartlands, one of the last realms of the elves in the North.
hill's edge: Hill's Edge was a small city on the Dusk Road, south of Anauroch on the River Reaching, south-east of Skull Gorge, east of Hardbuckler and west of the Sunset Mountains.
hluthvar: Hluthvar ( ) was a walled town on the Dusk Road in the Sunset Vale, east of the Reaching Woods and west of the Sunset Mountains. Hluthvar was named for a local warrior-hero.
iriaebor: Iriaebor ( ), also known as the Overland City and the City of a Thousand Spires, was a large city in Sunset Vale in the Western Heartlands region of west Faerûn.
myth drannor: Myth Drannor, formerly known as the city of Cormanthor ( ), the City of Song, For hundreds of years after the Weeping War, Myth Drannor languished as fiend-infested ruins.
scornubel: ), also known as the Caravan City, was a major tradestop for caravans. It lay on the northern bank of the River Chionthar, where the Trade Way reached the river.
secomber: {{Location It sat atop three stone hills on the northern banks of the southern-running Unicorn Run river and the western-running River Delimbiyr. Directly south of the town was the dangerous High Moor.
soubar: Soubar ( ) was a small village on the Trade Way, south of the Boareskyr Bridge and Forest of Wyrms, north of Scornubel. It was often used as a way-station for traders traveling along that road.
triel: Triel was a small village in the Fields of the Dead located at the intersection of the Trade Way and the Dusk Road, south of Boareskyr Bridge. The city of Elturel was located to the southwest and the Trielta Hills were located to the northeast.
griffon's nest: {{Location Throughout the years the Griffon's Nest was overseen by the great chiefs of the Griffon tribe, several of which were of the Bonesnapper line.
longsaddle: {{Location Situated east of the Crags and west of the Evermoors, Longsaddle sat on an isolated stretch of the Long Road. The surrounding area was a vast expanse of grassland that catered to the town's ranchers.
yartar: Yartar ( ) was a prosperous and increasingly crowded fortified city located in the Dessarin Valley region of the Savage Frontier. It was a member city of the Lords' Alliance, and held a number of allies throughout the North.
brost: {{Location Around 1370 DR, the town of Brost was an isolated trade town along the Tethir Road. Brost was widely known as a stop for merchant caravans and travelers and was well known enough across Tethyr to earn itself the moniker of "the Mushroom Village" by those in southern Tethyr.
llewellyn: {{Location It was a plain and prototypical Ffolk settlement. Several hundred cottages filled the town, surrounding a few larger structures including several inns and taverns.
easting: Easting might refer to: * Easting Reach, a wide expanse of water at the northeast of the Sea of Fallen Stars. * Easting River, a river in Northeast Faerûn that fed what remained of the Easting Reach after the Spellplague.
priapurl: ) was a small town located on the Trader's Road.
llorkh: {{Location Later on, further settlement of Llorkh and Loudwater, as well as Longsaddle, Secomber, Triboar, and others, was undertaken by pioneers from Waterdeep after the establishment of the Lords of Waterdeep there in 1032 DR.
everlund: Everlund was a city of merchant traders and caravan teams and was one of the greatest supporters of the league of the Silver Marches.
nesme: Nesmé ( ) was a small frontier city located in the Savage Frontier of northwest Faerûn. Nesmé sat beside the River Subrin. The dangerous Lurkwood forest rested in the north.
sundabar: {{Location Beneath Sundabar was a volcano rift known as the Everfire. Connected to the surface by a steep passage, the Undercity was home to most of the dwarven population.
highmoon: {{Location Highmoon was led by the Lord of Highmoon, who also served as the ruler over all of Deepingdale. By 1372 DR, this position was held by Theremen Ulath.
shadowdale: Shadowdale was a farming community in the Dalelands, in north Faerûn. It was the home of the archmage Elminster Aumar and was the home of two of the Seven Sisters, Storm Silverhand and Syluné.
dagger falls: Dagger Falls was a large, stone-walled town in the Daggerdale region of the Dalelands. The town was situated near a steep waterfall of the same name.
archenbridge:
{{Location ; The West Road
:Going northwest this road led to White Ford, away , and to the rest of the Dales through Arkhen Vale. As a result Archenbridge enjoyed a vibrant economy revolving around markets and merchant houses, the center of the town being as busy as Waterdeep at any hour of the day.
whitehorn: {{Location Whitehorn was located on the southern slopes of Whitehorn mountain, overlooking the steppes of the Ride. The trail of Rogan's Sprint connected the town to Verdigris, another small town about to the southeast at the base of the Dragonspine Mountains.
voonlar: Voonlar was a small farming town located between the Dalelands and the Moonsea. It was more urbanized than most farming communities because it was located at an intersection of trade routes.
glister: {{Location Due to its remote location in an otherwise desolate land, food and timber were its main imports, which were often traded for raw ores including iron, silver and copper.
valls: {{Location It was situated in the dusty plains of central Arcata—in western Damara—along a tributary to the Beaumaris River at the western end of the King's Road.
praka: {{Location Praka was known for its stout outer walls and mighty towers. Historically, House Praka was beloved by the citizens and the Baron of Ostel would even be appointed as Damara's steward during times of absence from the king.
ironspur: {{Location The city was a rugged settlement Ironspur was located on the edge of the Galena Mountains within the borders of the Duchy of Soravia in the Kingdom of Damara.
dragon falls: {{Location Though a small village, Dragon Falls was the biggest settlement on the North Road between Tsurlagol and King's Reach. However, the Dragon Falls themselves were actually a spring that cascaded over a bluff alongside the road and joined the Fire River.
laviguer: {{Location It lay in the Uplands of northwestern Impiltur, at the foot of the Earthspur Mountains, at the end of the Prince's Road.
nathlekh: {{Location It was originally populated by feline lycanthropes worshiping Nobanion and Sharess. It had a significant population of mundane cats (including lions) and its mysterious rulers were known as the Cat Lords.
cedarspoke: {{Location In , the neighboring kingdom of Turmish came to clash with the druids of Silvanus and the Emerald Enclave. The Windlass, the wizardly conclave that ruled Turmish at the time sent a part of their army to attack Cedarsproke.
xorhun: Xorhun, also known as Corellon's Cradle and Lifeblood Falls, was a special city in the Turmish area, on the edge of the Halondar Valley. This community of elves and gnomes hearkened back to the communities of the ancient elven civilization.
nathoud: {{Location Nathoud sat in the hill country at the feet of the southern slopes of the Icerim Mountains. Wood was used in the construction of Nathoud since stone-working was little known in the region.
kront: Kront was a small crossroads settlement and trade outpost situated where the Great Road intersected with the Cold Road on the plains of Ashanath in the Unapproachable East.
bezentil: {{Location Bezentil was situated along the Great Road, between the settlements of Uthmere and Kront. Local governance was overseen by a village council, led by Kassantra Mufdan, and law enforcement was carried out by Sheriff Trag Finstek and his handful of militiamen.
two stars: {{Location Two Stars was above sea level. Lady Yolatir Gallidy ruled the city from at least Her general style of rule did not involve sticking her nose into anyone's business, unless someone got hurt.
phent:
Phent was a fortress city in Thesk along the Golden Way. FR:Phent

amrutlar: During the 10 century, the city of Amruthar was ruled by the powerful Mulhorandi satrap named Sekhotet. When the Red Wizards fought for their independence from Mulhorand in 922 DR, Sekhotet joined their rebellion on the condition he could rule his city by his own will.
relkath's foot: {{Location A number of the city's inhabitants made their homes on wooden platforms hanging on the massive trees and the surrounding forest, strung together by a complex web of ropes and suspension bridges, on which outsiders were rarely permitted.
almorel: Almorel was a cosmopolitan yet primarily human trade city on the Golden Way. Almorel was located on the southeastern shores of the Lake of Mists where the Golden Way ran alongside it.
phannaskull: {{Location In lay on the north bank of the River Rauthenflow and at the end of a road from Delbyl. It was known as an ancient and rich city.
rauthil: {{Location Rauthil was located along the southern bank of the River Rauthenflow due north of Maerlar on the Great South Road in north Mulhorand. The precept of Rauthil in the , was a priest of Horus-Re named Ethnestus.
maerlar: {{Location Maerlar sat at the crossroads of the Great South Road, Great East Road, and the Road to the Dawn in north Mulhorand.
three swords: Three Swords was a fortified town on the upper side of the Landrise in the Eastern Shaar, circa the Year of Rogue Dragons, 1373 DR. It was destroyed as a result of the Spellplague in the Year of Blue Fire, 1385 DR.
kholtar: Khôltar was a small city on the edge of the Great Rift in south Faerûn. It was known as the Iron City because of its high walls covered in iron. and to Shaarmid on the Golden Road about to the west.
channathgate: {{Location The settlement sat near the River Channath at the eastern end of the Channath Vale between the Channathwood to the north and the Swagdar and the Forest of Amtar to the south.
kormul: {{Location The city was ruled by the Harlord, an intelligent and ruthless, but most importantly loyal, puppet ruler, installed by the local drow and yuan-ti traders.
lapalgard: {{Location It stood in the south of the realm, at the end of roads from Ithmong and Lushpool via Dungar, and faced the Dun Hills and the Bandit Wastes.
hardcastle: Hardcastle was a noble house of Cormyr. The family was loyal to the Obarskyrs.
reddansyr: ) was a small settlement found in the Dragon Coast region of central Faerûn. It had a well-earned reputation as an adventurers' town because it was a good source of information for such people.
caer corwell: Caer Corwell, also called simply Corwell or Corwell Town, was a small city It lay abandoned and in ruins as of the late 15 century DR. While little more than a fishing village for most of its existence, Caer Corwell was said to have grown intothe prettiest city in the Moonshaes prior to its fall into ru
manshaka: {{Location During the Darkstalker Wars of the next year, Sultan Pesarkhal abandoned Manshaka for Calimport, to become ruler of the entire unified county of Calimshan and beginning its Tenth Age as syl-pasha.
tulmon: {{Location This city-state stood on a long and low-lying rocky plateau known as the Shoulder of Lehreng, dominating the shallow and muddy Bay of Balefires.
yeshpek: {{Location Yeshpek was referred to by some as the City of Chains, due to its primary export. As for its proper name, a number of commentators and mapmakers in the lands north of Land of the Lions were known to misspell it on several occasions as Yeslipek.
mintar: {{Location It was connected to two roads, Darkhope's Road connecting it westward to the town of Kzelter and Tyrant's Road (renamed from "Coast Road", in reference to Teldorn) connecting it eastward to the city-state of Saelmur.
saelmur: {{Location The city-state was sat in a natural bay in the Lake of Steam, rising upwards to the crests of four hills, which were capped with various columns, towers, and spires.
ankhapur: {{Location There were a number of tressym in the city. Curiously, on the day before Highsummer each year, every tressym in the city mysteriously disappeared only to return three days later.
yhep: {{Location The economy of Yhep was based on seafood and jewelry exports. However, the most valuable part of the Yhevvan economy was the rare deep red pearls cultivated in the oyster beds in Yhep's territory.
theymarsh: Theymarsh was a port town on the Lake of Steam, part of the Border Kingdoms region of Faerûn. Theymarsh's closest neighbor to the south was the town of Yallasch, connected to Theymarsh by a minor road.
sheirtalar: {{Location thumb|right|250px|A map of Lapaliiya circa 1358 DR. thumb|right|250px|A map of Lapaliiya circa 1372 DR. Sheirtalar was a coastal city located on the eastern end of the Shining Sea, at the head of Sheir Bay, which was on the northern side of the larger Talar Bay at the foot of the Sheir Peninsul
lushpool: {{Location It stood on the Lapal Way, by the mouth of Talar Bay in the sheltered lee of the Ithmong Peninsula, where it faced the Shining Sea. In the Year of the Prince, 1357 DR, after four years of adventuring, Prince Royal Shaliim returned to Lushpool.
ithmong: {{Location Darromar, formerly known as Ithmong, was a metropolis and the capital of Tethyr. It lay on the River Ith. Its central location ensured that the queen's armies in 1479 DR were never more than five days' hard ride from any trouble in her domain.
lundeth: {{Location This village scaled the steep sides of a rock [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinnacle_(geology) pinnacle] surrounded by the Salt Flats and had a deep water well.
delselar: {{Location Delselar was founded on the southern border of the Guthland near the mouth of the Thingulph along the southern bank of the River Dolsel.
ishau: {{Location Periodically, sea hags navigated through the ruins looking for treasure or the remains of the dead. After it sunk, Ishau was home to reef and hunter sharks, along with aquatic dinosaurs called plesiosaurs.
port castigliar: Port Castigliar ( ) was a small settlement in Chult, tucked away in a rarely visited part of Refuge Bay. The settlements namesake, Castigliar was a wealthy nobleman from Scardale and uncle of Ilyber Kitcher, the explorer who named and settled this plot of beach.
port nyranzaru: {{Location Independent in the late 1480s or early 1490s Although independent in the mid-to-late 14 century DR, It was built atop four hills: Mount Sibasa, Temple Hill, Throne Hill, and Yklwazi Hill.
samargol: {{Location {{quote|They are a suspicious lot here, that's for certain – but have you ever seen such a city? Waterdeep is finer, certainly – but to be in the mysterious Samargol itself – now, that is something else!|Volothamp Geddarm to the immediate east from the Snout of Omgar at its base, and on the mouth of Rive
krenalir: Krenadir Krenadir was founded in 218 DR. During the height of the harvest season 100 warders protected the city and surrounding land.
ormpe: {{Location In , Ormpé was a rustic mining community. Gnomes were a common sight in the city. So was the Finglefall chaka. The field glass was an invention of the gnomes of the city.
assur: Assur was a small port city in Durpar. The city was destroyed by giants from the Beastlands but was rebuilt as a fortress city with a large garrison. The city had a deep harbor and a large market.
zindalankh: {{Location Zindalankh sat on the western rim of the Semphar Water within the southern portion of Gbor Nor. Around the , Martek departed from the city in a caravan headed for Medinat Muskawoon with the intention of stopping Khalitharius.
khalab: {{Location Khalab sat on the western banks of Gbor Nor. Though the village was unremarkable, some considered the long trip to Khalab well worth the effort with the hopes of training under Salid Dhuzma, a bard of great renown.
port ghaast: {{Location Situated along the western bank of the River Ghaast and the coast of Brightstar Lake, Port Ghaast was a prime military location for incursions into neighboring Semphar.
laothkund: Laothkund was a city in the Unapproachable East, on the coast of the Sea of Fallen Stars. It was later known as Laothkund the Drowned after it sank into the sea.
emmech: {{Location The fortress was originally named Emmech, and was built by King Brindor Olósynne to aid in the defence of Aglarond against invaders from Thesk.
uthmere: {{Location Following the receding of the sea, most of the townsfolk fled to Impiltur. The remaining villagers, as well as the farmers of the surrounding lands, were known to treat outsiders fairly.
ylraphon: ), also known as Yrlaphon, was a town in the Vast, lying on the eastern shore of the northern end of the Dragon Reach, at the western end of the Hunt Trail. Elves from Cormanthor went beyond the River Lis to found Yrlaphon among the eastern woodlands in .
harrowdale: {{Location Inhabitants of Harrowdale were known as Harrans, sometimes also Harrovans or Velarr, and as of 1368 DR, were primarily farmers and foresters.
scardale: {{Location The main feature of the dale was the massive chasm known as the Scar, which enveloped the River Ashaba as it poured into the Sea of Fallen Stars. While this tributary formerly had the most concentrated population of Dalesfolk, as well as housed its largest city, it waned in importance over the years.
yhaunn: Yhaunn ( ) was a coastal city of Sembia built on an ancient quarry site. The oldest city in Sembia, Yhaunn was a small but lively place that was quite different from the other major cities of the realm.
ilipur: {{Location Ilipur had a shallow harborage with no real docks. Trade ships' cargoes needed to be unloaded onto flat barges and dragged to shore. New ships were constructed on land and pushed into the sea as the town did not have dry docks.
samra: Samra is a small fishing town in Chondath. Samra was a relatively small fishing town. It had few defenses and no walls. The city had docks, but they were unaccommodating for bigger vessels, leaving Samra deprived of a huge part of the trade in the Vilhon Reach.
airspur: Airspur was the capital of Akanûl. The city was located on two cliffs facing a narrow bay. Many buildings were located on earthmotes that floated over the bay and were connected to each other and the cliffs by bridges.
soonenar: Soorenar was a city-state located on the western coast of the Bay of Chessenta that headed the Northern Alliance, one of the three most powerful alliances in Chessenta as of the mid-to-late 14 century DR.
dragonspear castle: {{Building Dragonspear Castle was built across three low hills on the southwestern edge of the High Moor, east of Trollbark Forest and just north of where the Coast Way joined the Trade Way.
warlock's crypt: {{Location As a Netherese enclave, the city was originally named "Orbedal" and was also called "Sanctuary". Under the rule of Larloch, the city was called variously "Larloch's Crypt" Warlock's Crypt lay somewhere in the western side of the Troll Hills, at the mouth of the Winding Water.
durlag's tower:
{{Location thumb|right|250px|A map of Durlag's Tower and the surrounding area.
The fortress was located south of the Wood of Sharp Teeth, a couple of miles from the small settlement of Gullykin.
castle tethyr: Castle Tethyr was once the palace of the royalty of Tethyr before its fall The entire square castle covered an area of about with about per side. It had three stories and had a subterranean dungeon.
mines of tethyamar: {{Location Early trade in Tethyamar was primarily with its nearest neighboring realms. These included Anauria, Asram, Avaeraether, Cormanthyr and Hlondath.
bell in the deep: {{Location Northkeep was a great and magical city, and it was while under the protection of those magics that humanity began to press back the orc hordes and take command of the sea.
delhalls: {{Location Deep within the twisting tunnels was a vault sacred to Auril and said to contain some great treasure or artifact belonging the Ice Queen Iyraclea.
castle perilous: {{Building It was a fortress of dark stone and bound in iron. Prior to its destruction, Castle Perilous was a tall and narrow tower that rose high above the wasteland and could be seen for miles.
talagbar: Talagbar was a dwarven mine in eastern Vaasa. It was considered a "twin" of the Delhalls in western Vaasa. Talagbar was located in the Galena Mountains to the east of the road from Nigel's Ford to Palischuk.
clymph tower: {{Building The Nar demonbinder Clymph built the proud walled keep of Clymph Tower in the , as a pen for his foul minions, the demons that he had summoned and bound to his will.
winterkeep: Winterkeep was a ruin located on the southern tip of the Yal Tengri. East of Winterkeep were the Glittering Spires. On the surface, only rubble remained, but the extensive subterranean passageways and chambers remained mostly intact.
dalelost: {{Location Once upon a time, this settlement was a competitor of Yhep for much of the local pearl trade. Despite its prosperity, over the course of a decade several disasters and misfortunes—the nature of which was forgotten to history—left Dalelost in ruins and abandoned by its people.
lhesper: Lhesper was a ruined town on the shore of Lake Lhespen in the western region of the Shaar. Lhesper was founded in the , by refugees from Lapaliiya who were fleeing plague.
city of shade: {{Location On Toril, Thultanthar was located in the middle of the Anauroch desert along the Black Road trade route connecting the Silver Marches with Cormanthor, in the area of the Bedine tribes.
thindar: {{Location Thindar was located in the center of Thindol along the northwestern shores of the Thingulph. Thindar was an unwalled city that sprawled across a marsh that had been filled in.
tashluta: {{Location The city was divided into a number of districts, including the wealthy districts of its mercantile families built atop the higher ridges of the Tashalar Basin, and the districts built beneath them that housed the city's lower and middle class citizens.
chavyondat: Chavyondat was a port city and the capital of Estagund. It was the largest city in that realm. Chavyondat was formerly known as Klionna. Situated on the protective Bay of Kings on the southern coast of Estagund, Chavyondat was the first line of defense against raiders from Dambrath.
vaelan: {{Location The Tower District, Vaelan's central district, held over 100 slender white-plastered towers full of balconies, galleries and promenades; they were home to the city's nobility.
heliogabalus: {{Location Helgabal was located in central Damara, and sat on the northwestern shores of Lake Mogador at the mouth of the Goliad River. It lay within the borders of the Barony of Morov at a central point along the King's Road.
velprintalar: Veltalar (formerly Velprintalar) was a settlement in Aglarond and the nation's primary port in 1479 DR, with a population of around seventy thousand. It was founded by human colonists from Chessenta in 756 DR.
murghyr: {{Location Murghyr was located in western Murghôm on the east bank of the River Murghol where it joined the River Rauthenflow just south of the Ganathwood near the border of Mulhorand.
goldenfields: Goldenfields, nicknamed the Granary of the North, was a walled abbey to Chauntea of spectacular scope and size. It was the most prolific provider of crops, grains and fruits to the people of the North.
grandfather tree: {{Person Grandfather Tree stood over tall and had a base measuring in diameter. Around the tree were two rings of raised earth. The innermost ring had four normal-sized oak trees, healthy and mature, growing out of it.
monastery of the yellow rose: {{Location The Citadel of the White Worm was an immense and sprawling fortress. From the outside, it projected many turrets, balconies, and windows.
well of dragons: {{Location thumb|right|300px|A map of the Well of Dragons, circa the 1480s DR. The citadel was built at the bottom of the caldera of a once-active volcano.
mount talath: Mount Talath was the name of one of the tallest mountains in the western half of the Nathaghal range of Halruaa. It was the site of the High Temple of Mystra and one of the largest collections of magic in all Faerûn.
citadel adbar: Citadel Adbar was a dwarf fortress-city in the Silver Marches. It was named for King Adbar, the ancient dwarf who began its construction in the and completed it in .
citadel felbarr: {{Location The badge of office for the King of Citadel Felbarr was a simple golden crown adorned with three large sapphires. Citadel Felbarr was located at the base of the Rauvin Mountains along the River Redrun, with Silverymoon Pass to the south and Sundabar Vale to the east.
darkhold:
{{Building Image:Darkhold 4e.jpg|4e
Image:Darkhold.jpg|2e The Darkhold was situated on the side of the mountain known as the Grey Watcher, within the Sunset Mountains of the Western Heartlands.
iron keep: {{Location {{Quote|With this secure base to operate from, let us prepare our ships for trade. Are we not the greatest sailors in the world? Our vessels can carry goods from any realm known to man, to any other realm.
irphong: This lifeless island was used as a marker to show the northern end of Asavir’s Channel. It's only notable feature is one of the Sea Towers was built on the cliff face of the north shore, 150 feet above the sea.
tower threespires: {{Building At a distance, this ruined wizards tower looked like a giant three-fingered hand reaching out of the Dunwood towards the sky.
